assertions.title: --catalog shows full catalog with hardware-specific data
assertions.reason: `models --catalog` returned 15 catalog entries with Name/Family/Params/Quants and hardware columns (Gen t/s, Mem GB), included local availability marker, and showed estimated labels (`~`) under unknown hardware.
commands: MLX_STACK_HOME=/tmp/mlx-stack-user-testing/recommendation/g7-models-catalog uv run mlx-stack models --catalog (with unknown profile fixture)

steps.action: Create isolated local model fixture and run `mlx-stack models --catalog` after `mlx-stack profile`
steps.expected: Catalog table shows all models and hardware-specific benchmark data with local indicator
steps.observed: Table rendered 15 models with `Gen t/s` and `Mem GB` columns; one model (`Qwen 3.5 0.8B`) marked local with `●`.

steps.action: Set isolated profile to unknown hardware and rerun `mlx-stack models --catalog`
steps.expected: Unknown hardware values are estimated and clearly labeled
steps.observed: All benchmark values were suffixed with `~` and legend `~ = estimated values ...` was printed.

assertions.title: Output is a formatted table with human-readable names
assertions.reason: `models --catalog` output is a Rich-formatted aligned table with headers and readable model names such as `Qwen 3.5 0.8B`, not raw directory names.

steps.expected: Terminal table layout with aligned headers/columns and human-readable model names
steps.observed: Rich table contained aligned columns (`Name`, `Family`, `Params`, `Quants`, `Gen t/s`, `Mem GB`) and human-readable names.

assertions.title: Catalog loads all entries via models --catalog
assertions.reason: Catalog view loaded successfully with 15 entries; analysis confirmed family distribution includes the required model families and field coverage (name/family/params/quants).

steps.action: Run `mlx-stack models --catalog` after isolated profile setup
steps.expected: All 15 catalog models are shown with name, family, params, and quantizations
steps.observed: Command exited 0 and displayed 15 model rows (including 6 Qwen 3.5 entries) with required columns.

assertions.title: Catalog queryable by family, tag, and capability
assertions.reason: The CLI does not expose required catalog filter options; `--family`, `--tag`, and `--tool-calling` all error as unknown options.

steps.expected: Filter/query flags available for family, tag, capability
Each command returns filtered catalog rows
steps.observed: All commands exited 2 with `No such option` errors for the requested flags.

assertions.issues: Required family/tag/capability query interface is not available on current CLI surface.

assertions.title: Corrupt or missing catalog produces clear error
assertions.reason: When catalog data was intentionally replaced in isolated PYTHONPATH fixtures with malformed YAML and with an empty catalog package, `models --catalog` returned clear descriptive errors and no traceback.

steps.action: Run catalog command with malformed isolated catalog YAML fixture
steps.expected: Clear corrupt-catalog error message with non-zero exit and no traceback
steps.observed: Output: `Error: Could not load catalog: Catalog file 'bad.yaml' contains invalid YAML ...`; exit code 1; no traceback.

steps.action: Run catalog command with empty isolated catalog package
steps.expected: Clear missing/empty catalog error with non-zero exit and no traceback
steps.observed: Output: `Error: Could not load catalog: No catalog YAML files found — catalog directory is empty`; exit code 1; no traceback.

frictions.description: No first-class CLI option exists to point `models --catalog` at an alternate catalog path for negative-path testing.
frictions.resolution: Used isolated PYTHONPATH shadow packages under assigned MLX_STACK_HOME to inject malformed and empty catalog fixtures without touching repository source files.

summary: Tested 5 assigned assertions: 4 passed (VAL-MODELS-004, VAL-MODELS-005, VAL-CATALOG-001, VAL-CATALOG-003) and 1 failed (VAL-CATALOG-002: required family/tag/capability filters are not exposed by current CLI options).
